name: Cost structure

subjectOf.text: Prior work shows that registration and the increased compliance requirements under the Dodd-Frank Act only marginally increase the cost structure of hedge funds.
subjectOf.abstract: requirements under the Dodd-Frank Act marginally increase the cost structure of hedge funds (Kaal [2013]).
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Impact of Dodd-Frank Act Compliance Cost on the Hedge Fund Industry (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389423
scope_conditions: hedge funds subject to Dodd-Frank Act registration requirements

subjectOf.text: Between 2012 and 2015 the annual cost of Dodd-Frank compliance doubled for many survey respondents, moving from the $50,000 to $100,000 range into the $100,000 to $200,000 range.
subjectOf.abstract: In fact, the data suggest that the annual cost of compliance doubled for many survey respon- dents, moving from the $50,000 to $100,000 range to the $100,000 to $200,000 range.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Post Dodd-Frank Act Evolution of the Private Fund Industry Comparative Evidence from 2012 and 2 (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2739479

subjectOf.text: Associated with the lack of an existing product is the inability of most crypto platforms to generate revenue to offset costs the way traditional businesses do, since they typically have neither employees who create and advertise a product nor customers who generate revenue.
subjectOf.abstract: Associated with the lack of an existing product is the inability of most crypto platforms to generate revenue to offset costs like traditional businesses.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Marco Dell'Erba, Initial Coin Offerings Emerging Practices, Risk Factors, and Red Flags (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3067615

subjectOf.text: The cost structure of centralized micro task systems, which require intermediation, produces significant overpricing that does not benefit the workers themselves.
subjectOf.abstract: First and foremost, the cost structure for micro task work in centralized systems that necessitate intermediation results in significant overpricing without benefiting the micro task workers directly.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900

subjectOf.text: Consensus by redundancy fails economically: multiplying the same work across many workers significantly increases the cost of micro task work.
subjectOf.abstract: The multiplication of work inherent in this process significantly increases the cost of micro task work.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized platforms using redundant task assignment

subjectOf.text: The protocol lowers cost because it removes the manual verification step and the associated multiplication of micro task work that centralized systems require, letting decentralized workers capture the gains from disintermediation.
subjectOf.abstract: the Semada Protocol removes the manual verification and the associated multiplication of micro task work necessitated by centralized systems, enabling its decentralized micro task workers to profit from the disintermediation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: micro task crowdsourcing under the Semada Protocol

subjectOf.text: Centralized platform fees charged to requesters for the right to submit tasks exert downward pressure on worker compensation, so the fee structure itself is what depresses pay.
subjectOf.abstract: Such centralized fees add downward pressure on the platforms' worker compensation.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralized Mechanical Turk Through Verified Reputation (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3128900
scope_conditions: centralized marketplaces such as Crowdflower and MTurk

subjectOf.text: When multiple firms trade the same securities in legacy systems, each maintains its own ledger, and that duplication is itself the source of increased operational risk and cost.
subjectOf.abstract: Legacy systems in which multiple firms are trading the same securities utilize multiple ledgers which increases operational risks and increases costs.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Blockchain-Based Securities Offerings (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411110
scope_conditions: multiple firms trading the same security

subjectOf.text: Network effects proliferate in peer-to-peer networks because, unlike client-server architecture with linearly increasing per-unit costs, peer-to-peer network costs decrease with each added node.
subjectOf.abstract: Network effects proliferate in peer-to-peer networks because, unlike the traditional client-server architecture which is subject to the linearly increasing per-unit costs, the peer-to-peer network costs decrease with each added node.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization and Feedback Effects (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808852

subjectOf.text: Digitization was the precondition for peer-to-peer transactions at scale, and the digital transformation of business enabled, for the first time in history, decentralized production at lower cost.
subjectOf.abstract: Digitization was a precursor to peer-to-peer transactions at scale. Correspondingly, the digital transformation of business enabled for the first time in history a form of decentralized production at lower cost.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859

subjectOf.text: Peer-to-peer architecture inverts the role of the audience: higher demand for a file produces more seeding nodes, which lowers the per-file delivery cost, whereas in client-server architecture demand consumes bandwidth proportionally.
subjectOf.abstract: By contrast, in the peer-to-peer network, higher demand for a file triggers higher levels of seeding nodes for the high demand file. The higher seeding level for the file lowers the delivery cost for each distributed file.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859

subjectOf.text: A peer-to-peer computing architecture is more efficient than client-server because client-server carries linearly increasing per-unit costs while peer-to-peer costs fall with each added node, which also leaves the traditional architecture more exposed to competition.
subjectOf.abstract: The traditional client-server architecture is subject to the linearly increasing per-unit costs whereas with a peer-to-peer network, cost decreasse with each added node.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859

subjectOf.text: To form consensus and offset worker error, requesters in centralized micro task structures assign teams of up to fifteen workers to the same task, and the resulting multiplication of work significantly increases the cost of micro task work and produces waste when requesters pay proportionally for redundant output.
subjectOf.abstract: set up teams of up to 15 workers to perform the same task in an effort to form a consensus. The multiplication of work inherent in this process significantly increases the cost of micro task work.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI Learning - Decentralized Governance to Optimize Human Output Datasets for AI Learning (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4755632
scope_conditions: applies to centralized micro task platforms using redundancy for consensus

subjectOf.text: Because LER rewards are funded out of marketing budgets at roughly one to five cents per holder-day and expensed immediately under U.S. GAAP, the program avoids the balance sheet drag that conventional loyalty liabilities create.
subjectOf.abstract: LER avoids balance-sheet drags and streamlines finances by using marketing budgets at a modest $0.01–0.05 per holder-day and expensed upfront under U.S. GAAP.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards in Corporate America (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5583610
